features: SetWindowDisplayAffinity + WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE (Windows 10 v2004+): excludes the window from tested Windows screen-capture paths with zero visual artefact

invisible-window-research.fullDescription: A 13-page IEEE-format research paper documenting a structural vulnerability in WebRTC-based exam proctoring. Operating systems expose documented APIs, SetWindowDisplayAffinity on Windows and NSWindow.SharingType.none on macOS, that let an application exclude its window from tested screen-capture paths while remaining fully visible on the physical display. This challenges the trust assumption in capture-based proctoring. Proof-of-concept implementations achieved 100% evasion across tested Windows and macOS lab configurations, including macOS 26 where the attack was previously assumed mitigated. Configurations were simulated, not commercial proctoring products; macOS 26 used native CGWindowListCreateImage and screencapture rather than browser getDisplayMedia(), and Linux was not tested. Findings reflect the tested software versions as of March 2026 and may change after patches.
invisible-window-research.problem: Remote proctoring systems detect prohibited content by capturing the student's screen via the WebRTC getDisplayMedia() API. The implicit security assumption is that the captured frame faithfully represents the physical display. The research demonstrates a gap in that assumption: documented OS display APIs excluded windows in tested capture paths without privilege escalation or kernel modification. These findings concern controlled, simulated Windows and macOS configurations; they do not establish bypass of every browser or commercial proctoring product.
solution: Formalised the trust-boundary violation between the W3C Screen Capture API and the OS compositing pipeline
Surveyed SetWindowDisplayAffinity (Win32) and NSWindow.SharingType.none (macOS); both appear in official SDK references
Built proof-of-concept implementations in Win32 C (Windows) and Swift (macOS) demonstrating full screen-capture evasion

Evaluated simulated proctoring configurations in a controlled lab on Windows 10/11 and macOS 14–26; no commercial products were tested, and macOS 26 used native capture rather than browser getDisplayMedia()
Analysed which behavioural detection mechanisms (gaze tracking, mouse dynamics, process enumeration) can and cannot detect the attack
Proposed and assessed five countermeasures, ranging from deployable (flag enumeration) to long-term (hardware attestation)
Coordinated OS vendor disclosure: Microsoft MSRC (notified Feb 2026, classified Apr 2026) and Apple Product Security (notified and classified Mar 2026) both issued formal classifications
proof: 100% evasion rate across Windows 10/11 and macOS 14–26, measured over 10,000+ frames per configuration
Zero visual artefacts detected in captured frames (no black rectangles, compositing errors, or flicker)

Window exclusion remained effective in tested native capture paths on macOS 26.3.1 despite Apple's documented ScreenCaptureKit changes in macOS 15; no direct ScreenCaptureKit or browser getDisplayMedia() test was performed on macOS 26
Linux (X11/Wayland) was not evaluated; these results apply to the tested Windows and macOS configurations

Behavioural detection showed no significant effect at this sample size. Gaze tracking (p = 0.41, n = 8) was underpowered, and mouse dynamics fell within normal exam-behaviour variance. This does not establish that behavioural detection is impossible in all settings
Published as a Zenodo preprint under CC BY 4.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20376495), with 13 pages, 53 references, and IEEE conference formatting

project-simurgh.fullDescription: Project Simurgh is a sole-author, open-source research prototype for inspecting what an AI agent is permitted to do. Delegation, stop, lease and credential state are held on the host; each tool proposal is checked against that state outside the model. Signed Ed25519 evidence archives can be replayed offline. Its October 2026 transfer study reports a benefit on one model and a null result on another. Earlier classifier-miss and AgentDojo results remain separate frozen experiments, while the original device-integrity preprint records the project’s earlier research lineage.
project-simurgh.problem: A tool-using agent may propose actions after its delegation, stop, lease or credential state has changed. Host controls need to enforce that state outside the model. Evaluating those controls also requires matched baselines, useful-task outcomes and uncertainty reporting: an already-clean model baseline cannot demonstrate additional protection.
solution: Holds delegation, stop, lease and credential state on the host, checks every tool proposal outside the model, and signs replayable evidence with Ed25519

October 2026 transfer study: 24 tasks, two trials each, three matched controls (credential-only, composed, deny-all), two models and 288 replayed branches; protocol to published package took 15–17 October 2026
On Meta Llama-3.2-3B, composed host controls cut restricted-state trials with new effects from 17/24 to 0/24, retained 23/24 useful completions and blocked no valid proposal
On OpenAI gpt-6-luna the baseline was already 0/24; the study reports no incremental protection on that model
Reports uncertainty per state: 24 restricted trials form six states; Wilson 95% intervals are 43.6–97.0% versus 0.0–39.0%, and part of the gap holds by construction
proof: October 2026 matched-control transfer study: 24 tasks × two trials × three controls × two models; 288 replayed branches. The positive Llama-3.2-3B result and null gpt-6-luna result are reported together
Llama-3.2-3B: restricted-state trials with new effects 17/24 → 0/24, useful completions 23/24, no valid proposal blocked; gpt-6-luna: baseline 0/24, no observed incremental protection
Cluster scope: the 24 restricted trials occupy six states. Per-state Wilson 95% intervals are 43.6–97.0% versus 0.0–39.0%; part of the difference holds by construction

OpenAI Responses API integration defect: a role-placement error caused 8/8 workflow declines. Original traces were retained; a frozen developer-role correction completed 2/3 authorised workflows and declined 5/5 restricted workflows, with one refusal still open

Earlier frozen classifier stage (2026): real Llama Guard 4 12B over 180 cases; containment evidence covered all 138/138 malicious cases it missed, including 120 downstream injections outside an input-only classifier’s view. This is a coverage claim, not a classifier ranking

Earlier frozen AgentDojo stage (2026): self-hosted Llama-3.3-70B on 140 pre-registered workspace injections, targeted attack success 9/140 → 0/140; the deterministic four-suite run scored attack success 0/949 with unattacked utility 949/949. Both are scoped as small experiments
39 Lean 4 proofs behind a gate that rejects unproven “sorry” placeholders; 5,171 tests passed in the 19 October 2026 smoke run; 92 releases; one-command offline replay; AGPL-3.0
Audited 919 project documents and published all 141 dated findings, including overstatements in earlier closeouts, in the README
Current software archive DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21737792 is separate from the original device-integrity preprint DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20374849 and the other published preprints

project-zurvan.fullDescription: Project Zurvan is a local-first LLM knowledge engine that turns raw documents into a linked, searchable, git-friendly wiki, then exposes that wiki to AI agents via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Inspired by Andrej Karpathy's personal knowledge management gist, Zurvan is designed for researchers, engineers, and agents that need structured long-term memory without cloud lock-in.
project-zurvan.problem: LLM agents lack persistent, structured memory that survives between sessions. Existing RAG pipelines either require cloud infrastructure or lose the relational structure of knowledge: which claim supports which decision, which concept contradicts another. A local-first solution needs to ingest arbitrary documents, preserve knowledge relationships as a graph, and present the result to agents in a queryable, privacy-preserving format.
solution: Built a local document ingestion pipeline (MD, PDF, TXT, images) feeding a SQLite-backed knowledge store
The LLM extraction layer produces typed nodes for claims, concepts, entities, and decisions. The knowledge set grows as the corpus grows
Hybrid FTS5 + semantic search with graph-neighbour expansion surfaces deep context bundles for agent prompts
MCP stdio server exposes zurvan_search, zurvan_context, zurvan_remember, zurvan_decision_add, and graph tools to Claude Code and Cursor
Multi-project federation manages independent vaults with cross-vault search, contradiction detection, and policy drift radar
proof: 218 tests passing across 18 completed development phases
MCP server verified with Claude Code and Cursor client setup guides

divan-open-day.fullDescription: Divan is a bilingual Persian-poetry experience built for a Persian Society Open Day stall. A visitor selects Hafez or Rumi, holds an intention, and receives a single reviewed verse with its English translation, source attribution, and optional recitation. The app works offline after its first load and is privacy-first by construction: no cookies, trackers, backend, or visitor input, so it runs reliably on a venue's unreliable network while collecting nothing about the people who use it.
divan-open-day.problem: A public Open Day stall needs a fast, delightful cultural experience that works on unreliable venue Wi-Fi, respects visitor privacy completely, and treats Persian poetry with cultural and scholarly integrity: no hallucinated verses, no rasterised calligraphy, no data collection.

proof: No cookies, trackers, or backend are used. sessionStorage holds only public poem IDs

Tested across unit, component, accessibility, offline, share, performance, and security suites (Vitest) plus Playwright Chromium e2e

aion.fullDescription: Aion is an AI-powered Bible companion that lets users ask questions about scripture in plain language. Responses are grounded in actual Bible data retrieved via a Hybrid RAG pipeline combining keyword matching and semantic vector search (pgvector), then streamed in real time via SSE from Gemini. The app runs on mobile (React Native + Expo) and desktop (Tauri v2).
aion.problem: Bible study tools are either keyword-only search engines that miss semantic meaning, or AI chatbots that hallucinate verses. Users need conversational AI that is genuinely grounded in scripture with verifiable citations.
solution: Built a Hybrid RAG pipeline combining regex-based keyword extraction with OpenAI embedding (1536-dim) + pgvector semantic search
Implemented real-time SSE streaming from Gemini via Supabase Edge Functions
Designed rich inline verse cards with full book/chapter/verse attribution for verifiability
Added cross-platform support: React Native for mobile + Tauri v2 for native desktop
proof: Hybrid RAG retrieves source scripture for citation checking; the reported 40-question pilot does not guarantee hallucination-free answers
IP-based rate limiting (5/min burst, 30/3hrs, 200/day) with fail-closed defaults
Exact-match response cache eliminates redundant LLM costs
Anonymous authentication with no sign-up; Supabase RLS applies to all tables
